commit.message:
test(saves): cover newest-first directory order in the late-link case (#2888)

**What this is for:** keep the late-link regression from #2832 effective
on both creation-order and newest-first directory listings, as its
author asked for on that pull request (the review found the same weak
spot).

## What changed

In the case "a link to an entry that moves too", half of the 36 absolute
links are now made before `save/` exists and half after. Every existing
assertion and every link stays; no product code changes.

## How it was tested

Arch Linux, GCC 16.2.1 and Clang 23.1.3. The new test against the
product source from before #2832 (`76101111`) and against main
(`3723fd0b`), 30 runs a cell, passes/failures:

| Product source + new test | btrfs GCC | btrfs Clang | tmpfs GCC |
tmpfs Clang |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Before #2832 | 0/30 | 0/30 | 0/30 | 0/30 |
| Current-main base | 30/0 | 30/0 | 30/0 | 30/0 |

- Listed unsorted, btrfs (creation order) and tmpfs (newest first) each
put 18 of the added links before `save` and 18 after it. With #2832's
own test the old code failed only on btrfs; now it fails on both.
- This does not guarantee a late link for arbitrary hashed/name order; a
name-hash model can still put every link before save. The added names
retain broader coverage, not a guarantee.
- The project's workflow, run on my fork before opening this:
`tests/test_linux_saves_move.py` passes on Ubuntu and is skipped cleanly
on Windows as before; [the
run](https://github.com/mooki000/Hookshot/actions/runs/43276384898) is
red only in two tests that are red on main itself today
(`test_readme_menu_rows.py`, fixed by #2857; `test_wb_shadow_remake.py`
on Windows, fixed by #2868).
- Complete game-free suite here: 500 passed, 2 failed, 20 skipped. The
two: `test_readme_menu_rows.py` (main's, as above) and the updater
digest check (a .NET reference pack this PC lacks).

**Not measured:** ext4/xfs or other real filesystem orders; Windows,
where this check skips; a real game's first-start migration or real
saves.

Refs #2832.
